title: Use compatibility rendering before final React renderer rebuilds
decision: Markdown, CFR, compliance, and artifact output should first be ported through a live compatibility renderer, then high-value surfaces can be promoted into polished React components after the browser shell is stable.
context: The old EPP browser renderer has many edge cases across Markdown, CFR pages, compliance links, artifact blocks, placeholders, anchors, draft-review lenses, and editing affordances. The user agreed that restoring the full browser shell/navigation comes first and later clarified that compatibility should not mean pre-rendering the full corpus as a static build artifact.
rationale: A live compatibility renderer lets Archivist regain document coverage quickly from canonical source, including Appendix A and other edge-case EPP content, while preserving a future path to native React components for the surfaces that prove valuable.
alternatives_considered: Rebuild all Markdown and artifact rendering directly as final React components before full EPP browsing is restored
Keep the old generated HTML browser as the long-term renderer
Only render simple Markdown until each artifact family is redesigned
consequences: SG-0014 remains blocked by SG-0013 but no longer needs renderer-strategy grilling
The first renderer pass can prioritize live behavior parity and coverage over component polish
High-value artifact families can be promoted to React components after usage and review prove the need
